2_Introduction: The device showed the highest certified PCE of 9.0112%, with VOC of 0.0017 V, JSC of 20.931 mA/cm², and FF of 24777.0%.The device shows a maximum PCE of 9.0112%, with an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 0.0017 V, a short-circuit current density (JSC) of 20.931 mA/cm², and a fill factor (FF) of 24777.0%. The perovskite solution (1.6 mol/L) was prepared according to chemical formula of Cs0.1FA0.9Pb1I2.8Br0.2. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated onto the substrate at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then 5000 rpm for 30 s. During the spin-coating process, 120 µL of CB was dropped on the perovskite 10 s prior to the end of the second procedure. The film was subsequently annealed at 110 °C for 45 min. Image analysis shows that the spin-coating coverage reaches 98.3%, and the average grayscale value of the film is 16.2257.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-precision perovskite crystallization process, employing a 1.6 M precursor solution of Cs0.1FA0.9Pb1I2.8Br0.2 to balance tolerance factor and suppress halide segregation, was critically governed by the antisolvent engineering where 120 µL of chlorobenzene dripped 10 seconds before the end of the 5000 rpm spin-coating stage precisely quenched the nucleation, while the subsequent 110°C annealing for 45 minutes facilitated robust grain growth and reduced metastable intermediates. The resulting film's exceptional morphological uniformity, directly evidenced by image analysis revealing 98.3% spatial coverage and a consistent average grayscale value of 16.2257, indicates a highly continuous, pinhole-free morphology that establishes unimpeded charge transport pathways and minimizes shunting losses. This optimized microstructure and crystallization control culminated in the reported device performance parameters, including a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 9.0112%, an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 0.0017 V, a short-circuit current density (JSC) of 20.931 mA/cm², and a fill factor (FF) of 24777.0%.
